endorsements.quote: AI-supported rehabilitation recommendations should be reviewed and validated by qualified healthcare professionals; roles and responsibilities for AI use should be clearly defined; AI outputs and clinician decisions should be documented in the clinical record.

Patients and/or caregivers should be informed about the involvement of AI in rehabilitation decisions; AI-supported interventions should be adapted to patient preferences, functional status, and goals of care; proportionality between expected benefit and burden should be regularly reassessed.

Clinicians should have access to understandable and clinically meaningful explanations of AI outputs; documentation of data sources, model purpose, and updates should be available; AI involvement in clinical decisions should be transparent to patients and care teams.

The emphasis on human oversight, proportionality, and explainability suggests that AI-supported rehabilitation tools should be integrated as adjuncts to clinical reasoning, not as substitutes for professional judgement.

AI-supported rehabilitation systems should be evaluated for potential bias affecting palliative care populations; inclusive design and deployment strategies should be considered and prioritised; outcomes should be monitored to detect and address inequitable effects.

Healthcare organisations should provide or support ongoing training in AI literacy and ethics; clinicians should be supported in understanding AI limitations and appropriate use; multidisciplinary forums for ethical reflection and governance should be encouraged.
Guideline 5: The informed consent of the patient and/or carer must be obtained.

unlisted_practices: Reassess patient preferences, tolerance, and proportionality of benefit and burden on an ongoing basis as clinical trajectories evolve when using AI in palliative care.
Establish escalation pathways for when AI outputs and clinician judgement conflict.
Establish multidisciplinary forums for ethical deliberation on AI use.

screen.reason: This paper presents a normative policy analysis/framework deriving ethical-regulatory guidance for deploying and governing AI in palliative care rehabilitation.
